note: DERIVED, not authored. Generated from RELEASE-2.8.2-TRACKER.md and RELEASE-2.8.2-DEFECT-REGISTER.md by status/build-platform-board.js. Those documents are what a release is certified against and they win every disagreement, and this view is stale by at most one run. Re-run the generator after editing either document.

phaseBreakdown.note: Phase counts cover items NOT YET DONE (OPEN + WIP + BUILT + DECISION). FIXED and CLEARED items are assigned to NO phase, which is why the phase totals do not approach the release total. BUILT means implemented and awaiting certification - it is NOT outstanding work.

legend.FIXED: Implemented and verified. Tracker verdict DONE or MET.
legend.BUILT: Implemented, not yet certified by a full release run. Tracker verdict PARTIAL, BUILT or IN PROGRESS — the code landed, the suite that would prove it has not run.
legend.OPEN: Confirmed, not started. Tracker verdict TODO, or a defect nobody marked closed.
legend.DECISION: Blocked on an owner decision or an owner action. Tracker verdict BLOCKED or DEFERRED, or a TODO the tracker marks as the owner's.
legend.CLEARED: Not applicable — the premise was false, or the item is counted against another row. Tracker verdict N/A.
legend.ON HOLD: Parked, and NOT actionable by us. Blocked on something the owner has declined or cannot do yet, such as a paid plan tier or an external dependency. Tracker verdict HELD, ON HOLD or PARKED. Distinct from DECISION, which is waiting on an owner ANSWER we have asked for.
legend.STANDING: A rule, bar or definition that binds every session and has no completion condition. Never active work and never done. Tracker verdict STANDING.

directives.text: No Vercel preview deployments. Every non-main deployment must land CANCELED — CANCELED is free, BUILDING/READY/ERROR is billed.
A push is the only Actions-consuming action a push approval covers. Reruns, workflow_dispatch, a second push or a non-draft PR are each a fresh ask.
A commit hash AND a verification that ran AND a user-invocable outcome. Two of three is not done.
A gate that cannot fail is not a gate. Prove it fails before trusting that it passed, and take exit codes from UNPIPED commands.
A record of a thing is not the thing. Measure the artefact, not the comment, filename or tracker row describing it.
This board is DERIVED from the release tracker and defect register. Where they disagree with it, THEY WIN.

MANDATORY for every release, every session: start by reading this board. Be able to state total raised, how many are done, and of the rest how many are not started / written-awaiting-certification / awaiting an owner decision — INCLUDING which population each number belongs to. The headline counts and the per-phase counts measure different things; subtracting one from the other gives a wrong answer.

At release close every item goes to exactly ONE place: still pending (not started, built, or awaiting a decision) HANDS OVER to the next release with its evidence; done and cleared are SAVED AS RELEASE DELIVERY. The board then re-points at the new release. Nothing is dropped at a boundary. See docs/STATUS-BOARD-CHARTER.md.

If a status cannot express the truth, ADD THE STATE — never pick the nearest wrong one. Twice this release a status was falsified by a missing word: built-but-not-shipped read as FIXED, and withdrawn read as OPEN forever. A phantom OPEN is as damaging as a phantom FIXED.
crowagent-platform-web + crowagent-portal get FOUR Vercel production deploys for the whole release — ONE at each phase boundary. Nothing mid-phase, for any reason, including a docs-only commit.
crowagent-website is SEPARATE. It does not count against that budget and ships as and when ready.
Railway, staging AND production: deploy whenever needed. No approval, no waiting.
Supabase, staging AND production: apply whenever needed. No approval, no waiting. Via MCP apply_migration, never db push.
There is no Phase 5. Phase 2 is CLOSED. Every remaining item is Phase 3 or Phase 4.
Never report deploy or phase state from a repository document or git log. Read the live surface — Vercel, Stripe, Supabase, Railway.

notCounted: crowagent-website (marketing) — SEPARATE, ships as and when ready
Railway — staging AND production, unrestricted, never waits
Supabase — staging AND production, unrestricted, never waits

Importers measured per tree: web/lib 2 files which are the module and ITS OWN TEST, web/src 2 files which are both COMMENTS mentioning it rather than imports, web/app ZERO, apps/portal/src ZERO, packages ZERO. So it has NO production consumer anywhere, which is this codebase's signature defect applied to a security control. MEANWHILE, and this is why it matters rather than being tidy: apps/portal/src/lib/api/posthog-client.ts resolves its base from getCredential('POSTHOG_HOST'), an OPERATOR CONFIGURABLE value, trims trailing slashes and nothing else, then fetches it WITH authHeaders() attached, so the PostHog bearer token is sent to whatever host that value names. Not remotely exploitable by a customer, since it needs portal access, but it is precisely the shape the unused guard was written to prevent, and it becomes materially worse the moment provider configuration is widened as the owner asked. FIX: move the guard into packages/server-infra and route every credential derived fetch through it with a per provider host allowlist. This is the recommended FIRST step of any provider agnostic work, ahead of the features, because widening configurability without it widens this.

issues.title: [SEV:P0][LANE:PORTAL] publishing a regulation update reports success for an email fan out that is structurally impossible

THE CORE ROUTERS WERE DELETED: api/app/main.py:617 mounts only /api/v1/core/zapier under that prefix, so the target is a 404. The call sits in a try whose catch logs and then execution CONTINUES to return NextResponse.json with a published status. AND THE CATCH DOES NOT EVEN FIRE: fetch does NOT throw on a 404, it resolves with ok: false, and the response is never inspected. So the failure is invisible even in the log that was written to catch it. The operator is told the update was published and the emails queued. Nothing was queued and nothing can be. THIS IS WORSE THAN A STUB, because a stub does not assert an outcome. issues.title: [SEV:P1][LANE:SECURITY] a caller supplied Salesforce host receives the organisation's OAuth credentials
issues.note: FOUND 2026-09-08 while promoting the SSRF guard, REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED because the router sits outside that work's file ownership. It is the SAME defect as the PostHog client that row closed, in Python, and it is LIVE. api/app/routers/crm.py ConnectRequest.instance_url accepts a URL from the caller with no egress validation, and the stored value reaches app/services/crm_salesforce.py:136, which POSTs the organisation's Salesforce credentials to f'{self._instance_url}/services/oauth2/token'. So an operator supplied host receives an OAuth client secret and refresh token. This is worse than the eSourcing field that was fixed alongside it: there the exploitability was UNVERIFIED because the table held zero rows and no end to end fetch of the stored value was traced, whereas here the credential bearing fetch is written down and reachable. THE FIX IS ALREADY BUILT AND IS ONE IMPORT: api/app/schemas/safe_url.py now exports SafeExternalUrl and OptionalSafeExternalUrl, and the AST guard at api/tests/test_caller_supplied_url_fields_are_ssrf_guarded.py already ENUMERATES this field, so closing it is changing the annotation and removing the acknowledgement entry. Measured corpus at the time of writing: 10 caller supplied URL fields across app/routers, 4 guarded, and the other 6 named individually with a written reason rather than hidden behind a count. Needs a Railway deploy to take effect, which is not authorised.

issues.note: Cron and webhook callers carry no user JWT and stay on service_role by design. They are listed rather than converted, which is the part that must be written down or the guard becomes unpassable. [2026-09-21 RBAC SURFACE LANE, THE CONSISTENCY QUESTION THIS ROW LEFT OPEN IS NOW MEASURED ON THE WRITE PATHS FIRST.] WHAT THIS ROW HAD NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the application level .eq("organisation_id", org_id) filter is applied CONSISTENTLY on the converted routes, writes included. A read path that omits it leaks. A WRITE path that omits it lets one tenant mutate another, so writes were looked at first. SAMPLE: 40 distinct write chains (.update(, .delete(, .upsert() across 9 router files under api/app/routers/: crowmark/contracts.py 8, crowmark_answer_library.py 9, crowmark_evidence.py 7, crowmark/evidence.py 2, crowmark_collaboration.py 5, teams.py 1, api_keys.py 2, content_sources.py 4, crowmark_opportunities.py 2. RESULT: ZERO MISSES ON A WRITE PATH. 39 of 40 carry .eq("organisation_id", org_id) on the statement itself. The 40th, teams.py:1442 revoke_invite, is filtered by .eq("id", invite_id) alone, and is CLEAN because the SELECT at teams.py:1429 reads that same id with .eq("organisation_id", org_id) and 404s if absent, so the id is already known to belong to this org. IT IS FLAGGED ANYWAY AS THE ONE ASYMMETRY IN THE SAMPLE: it is the only chain relying purely on call graph ordering rather than defence in depth, which is exactly what the in-line reasoning at api_keys.py:301 and crowmark/contracts.py:1764 warns about, that deleting the read or reordering the handler removes the protection with nothing going red. Every table touched was confirmed to HAVE an organisation_id column against its CREATE TABLE migration, 13 tables, which is the check that separates a real miss from a table that cannot carry the filter. issues.title: [SEV:P1][LANE:SECURITY] removing a member deletes two membership rows and leaves the third, so the resolver still returns their organisation
issues.note: FOUND 2026-09-11 while measuring the membership drift row, and it is a REVOCATION THAT DOES NOT REVOKE. remove_org_member deletes the organisation_members row and the org_users row, and leaves profiles.organisation_id still naming the organisation. private.user_org_ids() unions a profiles branch, and its revoked exclusion CTE can only exclude an organisation that STILL HAS a membership row. A deleted row leaves none to exclude, so the profiles branch keeps returning that organisation and the removed person keeps READ access to every table scoped by the read resolver. Writes are not affected, user_org_ids_write() does not read profiles. The blast radius grew today: 49 CrowMark tables moved onto user_org_ids() for SELECT in migration 20269000000044, so this now reaches most of the product rather than a handful of tables. NOT EXPLOITABLE ON PRODUCTION TODAY, measured: one organisation, four users, nobody removed. It becomes live the first time a beta tester is removed. FIX IS ONE LINE, a UPDATE public.profiles SET organisation_id = NULL inside remove_org_member, prepared but NOT applied. Needs its own commit and a red proof that a removed member reads zero. Fixed with D10 in the same change. remove_org_member now clears profiles.organisation_id. Verified on production that the patched function body carries the new statement.

issues.title: [SEV:P1][LANE:PLATFORM] the team invite acceptance RPC is called with four arguments and exists with two, so accepting an invite has never worked
issues.note: FOUND 2026-09-11 while measuring the membership drift row. api/app/routers/teams.py:652 called accept_team_invite with {p_user_id, p_org_id, p_email, p_role}. The ONLY function of that name on EITHER database is public.accept_team_invite(p_invite_code text, p_user_id uuid), read from pg_proc on both projects, one row each. PostgREST resolves RPCs BY NAMED ARGUMENT, so this call cannot bind and the handler's except turns it into a 500. This blocked the entire beta onboarding path, because an invited tester could not join an organisation.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, and how a negative would have looked. shared/lib/proxy/onboarding-gate.ts answers with JSON only when expectsMachineReadableDenial(request, path) holds, and shared/lib/proxy/request-intent.ts requires an /api/ path AND a request that is not a top level navigation. isTopLevelNavigation reads Sec-Fetch-Dest, then Sec-Fetch-Mode, then Accept, and RESOLVES UNDECIDED TO TRUE. A client that sends neither Fetch Metadata header and an Accept of */* is therefore classified as a navigation and receives a 307 to /onboarding/organisation-type. The negative case is directly checkable: a client that sends Accept: application/json gets the 403 JSON, so the predicate is not broken, it is the DEFAULT that decides this. node_modules/playwright-core/lib/server/fetch.js:96 sets "accept": "*/*" on every APIRequestContext request and sets no Sec-Fetch headers, so onboarding-gate.spec.ts and abandon-resume.spec.ts both fall on the redirect side, and a 307 on a POST is followed with the method preserved onto a page route that has no POST handler. THE CONFLICT IS WITH A WRITTEN CONTRACT, not with my preference. lib/auth/requireOnboarding.ts exists, in its own words, because "a hand-crafted curl with a valid Supabase access_token would bypass that gate and hit the API directly", and it returns { ok:false, code:'NEEDS_ONBOARDING', redirect_to } at 403. The proxy now short circuits ahead of it for precisely that caller, so that defence in depth branch can no longer be reached by a curl, only by a fetch that declares JSON. R282-OBS-A's own comment predicted the behaviour and judged it harmless ("an unknown client therefore cannot be made worse by this predicate"), which is true as a comparison with the older behaviour and is not the

issues.title: [SEV:P3][LANE:E2E] the Discover feed test reads its row count from a page.on('response') body that came back unreadable, so a green feed was reported as an empty one
issues.note: THE INSTRUMENT WAS THE FAULT, AND IT WAS HIDING A SECOND, REAL ONE. The handler now records r.text() length and the caught error instead of discarding both through .catch(() => null) (crowmark-i-unexercised-journeys.spec.ts:95-119). Re-run against staging, project chromium, collected 2, 2 passed. With the body read as text and parsed, feedCount came back as 20, so await r.json() was failing where r.text() plus JSON.parse succeeds: the finding is the instrument exactly as the row predicted, and the BFF shape is fine. That immediately exposed the thing the null had been masking for a month: 20 in the payload against 19 carry links rendered. Not a dropped row. OpportunityFeed.tsx:344 defaults statusFilter to 'open', so a tender past its deadline is filtered out of lifecycleItems before the list renders, and the feed already states how many it removed in its own results line (ui-opportunities.ts:135, " · 1 hidden by status and deadline"). So carryLinks === feedCount was the WRONG DENOMINATOR, never a wrong idea. THE EQUALITY IS KEPT AND IT NOW PROVES MORE, NOT LESS: the assertion reads the shipped results line and requires carryLinks + hiddenByLifecycle === feedCount AND shown === carryLinks, so zero rendered rows still fails, and a silent drop between the API and the list now fails too, which the old form could not see. Nothing was softened, skipped or widened.

issues.note: FOUND BY CHECKING MY OWN DENOMINATOR, AND IT CORRECTS A CLAIM I MADE IN THE SAME SESSION. Closing R282-XR-PORTAL-APPROVE-PATH-STILL-RESOLVES-RAILWAY-FROM-ENV-ONLY-01 I reported that the three redeploy paths call resolveRailwayIdentity and that no fourth caller exists. That is true of the REDEPLOY paths and it is NOT true of Railway service identity, which is how I phrased it. A wider search I had abandoned mid-run came back afterwards and named a reader my scoped search never covered. CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, not by grep: app/api/railway/metrics/route.ts:203-206 calls getCredential('RAILWAY_SERVICE_ID') directly, so the Infra page's CPU, memory, request volume and p95 tiles resolve Railway identity outside the shared module. WHAT THIS IS NOT, measured rather than assumed, because the severity turns on it. It is a STORE read and not a process.env read, so it does NOT defeat the guard that row added, which asserts the absence of env only resolution, and the guard is not weakened by its existence. It is also read only, so unlike the three redeploy paths it cannot restart the wrong service and carries none of the production restart hazard that made the other row urgent. Its notConnectedResponse degrade is already correct and reports NULL rather than a healthy looking zero. WHAT IT IS: a second copy of the key NAME. It hardcodes the literal 'RAILWAY_SERVICE_ID' instead of reading RAILWAY_SERVICE_ID_KEYS from lib/integrations/railway-identity.ts, so it can only ever describe the PRODUCTION service and it will silently fail to see a key name added to that list later. That is the same drift shape that put three copies of the redeploy resolution in the tree, caught here while it is still only cosmetic. The negative case would have been this file importing the shared key list. It does not. NOT FIXED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUNDLED. THE CONFIRMATION IS THE ABSENCE OF A LINE: the fallback emits a structured warn naming which purpose is still borrowing the database credential, once per purpose per process, on every cold start. The two authorities it cites do not: web/tsconfig.json exclude is exactly ["node_modules", "**/*.test.ts", "**/*.test.tsx"] and .eslintrc.json boundaries/ignore is exactly ["**/*.test.ts", "**/*.test.tsx", "**/*.stories.tsx", "tests/"]. NEITHER NAMES .spec.*. So a .spec.ts under web/src IS inside the program next build compiles, boundaries/dependencies would flag it, and the vitest guard waved it through. A guard that backs up a rule cannot be looser than it. THE POPULATION IS ZERO TODAY AND THAT WAS EXPLICITLY REFUSED AS A REASON, because it is the same circular reassurance this change set had already rejected elsewhere. The new docstring says so in terms: "a zero count is trivially true of any exclusion and establishes nothing". THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDED IT IS WORTH KEEPING: the old justification cited vitests default include of /*.{test,spec}.*, which is TRUE but is about WHICH FILES THE RUNNER COLLECTS, a different property from WHAT THE PRODUCTION COMPILE CONTAINS, and only the second can justify an exemption. FIXED by NARROWING the predicate to .test.* rather than widening tsconfig.json, because narrowing makes a guard stricter and needs no justification while widening an exclusion always does. The .stories.tsx asymmetry was deliberately LEFT stricter for the identical reason and is now RECORDED rather than left to be rediscovered.
